svg.title: The Revolt of the Northern Earls (November–December 1569)
svg.desc: High-precision 1:10m GIS historical atlas map of Northern and Midland England and the Scottish Borders showing the November–December 1569 Revolt of the Northern Earls: Brancepeth Castle, Durham Cathedral Latin Mass, Hartlepool, Barnard Castle, Bramham Moor, Mary Stuart's transfer from Tutbury Castle to Coventry, the Earl of Sussex's royal army at York, and the rebel Earls' flight into Scotland.

text.tspan: KINGDOM OF SCOTLAND
Regent Moray • Protestant Ally of Elizabeth
KINGDOM OF ENGLAND
Loyal Gentry Stand by Queen Elizabeth I
NORTHERN EARLS’
HEARTLAND (Percy & Neville)
1. Brancepeth & Durham Cathedral (14 Nov 1569)
4,600 Rebels Tear Up English Bible & Restore Latin Mass
2. Hartlepool Seized (Late Nov 1569)
Alba’s Promised Spanish Troops Never Land
Barnard Castle Besieged (Dec 1569)
Sir George Bowes Holds Out 11 Vital Days
3. Rebel Advance South to Bramham Moor
Halt Near Tadcaster (24 Nov) & Retreat North
5. Earl of Sussex’s Royal Army at York
Reinforced by 12,000 Southern Royal Troops
4. Mary Stuart Moved: Tutbury → Coventry
Hurried South (25 Nov) to Foil Rebel Rescue
6. Earls Flee into Scotland (Dec 1569)
~450 Rebels Executed; Council of North Reshaped
